changedParagraphs.before: The Newmark permanent displacement Dn quantifies the displacement induced by an earthquake accumulates in the sliding mass and is the performance measure from which the seismic coefficients are derived. The Dn(ky) curves relate, for each combination of geometry, material, and design scenario, the yield acceleration ky to the expected permanent displacement; they were computed with an ensemble set of AM88 (Ambraseys & Menu, 1988), JB07 (Jibson, 2007), SR08 (Saygili & Rathje, 2008), BT07 (Bray & Travasarou, 2007), and BM19 (Bray, Macedo, & Travasauro, 2018), with the reference magnitude Mw = 7.0 and 300 realizations per demand and are read at the fractiles q=1-pe. The horizontal pseudostatic coefficient kh is in turn derived from the allowable permanent displacement Da of the potentially sliding mass (Bray & Travasarou, Pseudostatic Coefficient for Use in Simplified Seismic Slope Stability Evaluation, 2009; Macedo, Bray, Abrahamson, & Travasarou, 2018); the coefficients are reported at four relative displacement limits, Da/Hs = 0.1, 0.4, 1.0, 2.5%, and the tables in Section 10.3 and 11Appendix E report, for the demands and scenarios analyzed, the coefficient at each limit, expressed as a percentage of the PGA.
changedParagraphs.after: The Newmark permanent displacement Dn quantifies the displacement induced by an earthquake accumulates in the sliding mass and is the performance measure from which the seismic coefficients are derived. changedParagraphs.before: The PSHA for the Site was conducted using the OpenQuake v3.19.1 engine. Results of the PSHA are presented in terms of Annual Exceedance Probability (AEP) and Uniform Hazard Spectra (UHS) for site conditions ranging from hard to soft rock, as defined by the 2020 NBCC (Chapter 6). The analysis considers events associated with a target AEP of 1:475, 1: 975, 1:2,475, 1:5,000 and 1:10,000 years and for various confidence levels, including mean, 50th, 84th, 90th, and 95th percentiles.
changedParagraphs.after: The PSHA for the Site was conducted using the OpenQuake v3.26.2 engine. Results of the PSHA are presented in terms of Annual Exceedance Probability (AEP) and Uniform Hazard Spectra (UHS) for site conditions ranging from hard to soft rock, as defined by the 2020 NBCC (Chapter 6). The analysis considers events associated with a target AEP of 1:475, 1: 975, 1:2,475, 1:5,000 and 1:10,000 years and for various confidence levels, including mean, 50th, 84th, 90th, and 95th percentiles.

changedParagraphs.before: Dynamic site response analysis was used to modify the response spectra to the specific geotechnical conditions of each project facility (Chapter 6.5). This analysis involves estimating multi-period amplification factors dependent on the average shear-wave velocity of the upper 30 m of soil (Vs,30) as defined by the 2020 NBCC. Amplification factors were adopted from the from GMMs of the CanadaSHM6. Seismic Cone Penetration Tests (SCPT) conducted during the 2021-2022 and 2023 field investigations (SRK Consulting (Canada), Inc., 2023) (2024) provided Vs,30 values ranging from 180 to 230 m/s. A characteristic Vs,30value of 220 m/s was adopted for the site, classifying it as Stiff Soil Class D per the 2020 NBCC. The amplification factors were then applied to adjust the UHS for these site-specific conditions and were presented for target AEPs of ranging from 1:475 to 1:10,000 years and for various confidence levels.
changedParagraphs.after: Dynamic site response analysis was used to modify the response spectra to the specific geotechnical conditions of each project facility (Chapter 6.5). This analysis involves estimating multi-period amplification factors dependent on the average shear-wave velocity of the upper 30 m of soil (Vs,30) as defined by the 2020 NBCC. The design demands combine the direct logic-tree evaluation at each condition with the ST20 transformation of the demand at the reference condition of 760 m/s, conditioned on the PGA of the same realization. Seismic Cone Penetration Tests (SCPT) conducted during the 2021-2022 and 2023 field investigations (SRK Consulting (Canada), Inc., 2023) (2024) provided Vs,30 values ranging from 180 to 230 m/s. A characteristic Vs,30value of 220 m/s was adopted for the site, classifying it as Stiff Soil Class D per the 2020 NBCC. The resulting UHS for these site-specific conditions were presented for target AEPs of ranging from 1:475 to 1:10,000 years and for various confidence levels.

changedParagraphs.before: The 2020 NBCC offers an online seismic hazard tool that provides seismic hazard values for building design across Canada (Natural Resources of Canada, 2021d). A comparison of the mean response spectra from this tool with the PSHA analysis was conducted, covering the relevant AEPs and structural periods (Chapter 8). The results demonstrate that the PSHA analysis aligns with the seismic hazard estimations used in the 2020 NBCC tool.
changedParagraphs.after: The 2020 NBCC offers an online seismic hazard tool that provides seismic hazard values for building design across Canada (Natural Resources of Canada, 2021d). A comparison of the mean response spectra from this tool with the PSHA analysis was conducted, covering the relevant AEPs and structural periods (Chapter 8). The ratios of the PSHA spectral ordinates to the NRC 2020 values range from 0.70 to 1.30 for the periods and site conditions compared.

changedParagraphs.before: The Canadian Dam Association (CDA) (2013) along with the International Council on Mining and Metals (ICMM) (2020) and the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources (MNR) (2011), recommends performing PSHA and determining recurrence intervals based on the potential consequences of dam failure, which range from “Low” to “Extreme.” For this project, an “Extreme” consequence level has been designated for the FEED phase of the TMF, leading to a designation of the “Maximum Design Earthquake” (MDE) with an AEP of 1:10,000 years, consistent with GISTM and, for closure, with ICOLD and ANCOLD guidance. For the Clay, Rock, and Sand & Silt Impoundments, as well as the East and West Stockpiles, the MDE corresponds to an AEP of 1: 2,475 years. Response spectra and PGA values for the MDE have been provided for various site conditions, from hard rock to stiff soil, and at different confidence levels (Chapter 0). For stiff soils (Vs,30= 220 m/s), the MDE for the TMF is anticipated to result in a horizontal Peak Ground Acceleration (PGA) of 0.395 g (mean) and 0.491 g (84th percentile) and the MDE for the impoundments and stockpiles is anticipated to result in a PGA of 0.157 g (mean) and 0.198 g (84th percentile).
changedParagraphs.after: The Canadian Dam Association (CDA) (2013) along with the International Council on Mining and Metals (ICMM) (2020) and the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources (MNR) (2011), recommends performing PSHA and determining recurrence intervals based on the potential consequences of dam failure, which range from “Low” to “Extreme.” For this project, an “Extreme” consequence level has been designated for the FEED phase of the TMF, leading to a designation of the “Maximum Design Earthquake” (MDE) with an AEP of 1:10,000 years, consistent with GISTM and, for closure, with ICOLD and ANCOLD guidance.
